commits.message:
Move the await-free workflow fixtures out of the fixture module that awaits

The earlier fix covered one import; the dispute runner and the case history
still reached workflow.make-adapter.ts, whose load awaits two signed
transactions, so the node's es2020 emulator suite still failed to transform.
The release-finality authority, the accepting terminal verifier and the
fixture chain now live in two support modules with no await, and every
shared support module imports those. workflow.make-adapter.ts re-exports
them for the tests that use it directly.

Checked by walking value imports from all 16 exported test-support entries:
none reaches the awaiting module. tsc for fault-proofs and node: 0 errors.

Rename what was still named for the workflow journal

No fault-proof workflow keeps a journal, but names said otherwise.

- workflow/journal.ts re-exported workflow/journal.fraud-proof-workflow-
  terminal.ts; the one module is now workflow/identity.ts, and the package
  export is ./workflow/identity.
- JournalJson*, normalizeJournalJson and journalJsonDigest become
  WorkflowJson*, normalizeWorkflowJson and workflowJsonDigest;
  exactJournalRecord becomes exactArtifactRecord.
- one-step-staging-journal.ts becomes one-step-staging-types.ts and
  ValidationTraceStagingJournal becomes ValidationTraceStagings.
- The two timeout-correction modules named for recovering and reconciling
  an attempt hold the plan and the parameters and are named for those.
- The test helpers submit-unjournaled.* become submit-steps.*, and their
  functions lose the Unjournaled suffix.
- The watcher config key workflowJournalDirectory becomes
  decisionJournalDirectory: the directory holds the fault decision journal
  and the queue journal, which remain.

Deleted: the journal interfaces and loader fields of the two script-decoding
families, which nothing implemented or read.

496 files changed, 3932 insertions(+), 4734 deletions(-). Most changed lines are the formatter re-wrapping
shorter names.

Ran: tsc for fault-proofs, watcher, node and node-tools (0 errors); eslint
and prettier on changed files; module-size, doc-link, skill and
builder-export checks.

Delete the timeout-correction journal and the remembered removal

The unattested-block timeout correction kept an on-disk journal of its
attempts, with recover, supersede and reconcile steps, and the node recorded
each step in its intent journal. Every decision the journal made has a chain
answer: the target is the lock datum or the oldest timed-out header, a
landed step is a header gone from the queue, completion is an idle lock, and
the correction lock is a singleton every step spends, so the ledger admits
one attempt. Each run now reads the queue and the lock, builds the step they
call for and submits it. The node runs one step per head change; a tick
that meets a step still in flight is refused by the ledger and the next
tick reads again.

Removed with it: --correction-journal, the node's journal file and its
environment override, the correction family of the node intent journal, the
readiness progress count the chain cannot give, and the superseded-attempt
read schedule.

The network-id adapter no longer remembers the removal it submitted; the
raw-L1 route derives it from the chain and the provider route reports that
it cannot.

53 files changed, 229 insertions(+), 3288 deletions(-)

Ran: tsc for fault-proofs, node, watcher and node-tools (0 errors); eslint
and prettier on changed files; fault-proofs fast tier 6,959 passed, 0
failed, 3 skipped; watcher fast tier 1,553 passed; node fast tier 4,244
passed with two failures, one fixed here and rerun, one fixed in the
previous commit.
Not run: the node fast tier after those two fixes, the fault-proofs slow
tier beyond edited files, Docker and devnet suites. No test drives the
node's correction action end to end.

Keep top-level await out of the node emulator suite's import graph

The funded runner imported its terminal verifier from a fixture module that
awaits two signed transactions at load. The node suite compiles for es2020,
where that does not load, so validation-trace-defense-end-to-end-emulator
failed to transform. The runner builds the verifier itself.

Checked by bundling each node emulator test for es2020: no top-level await
error; the same bundle of the fixture module reports one.

Find our carriage outputs by content instead of remembering them

The CLI and direct step paths kept an in-memory map of the out-refs they
published and read their outputs back by it. Every caller now does what the
workflow already did: read the address and take the output whose content the
slot expects. Carriage sits at an address only the prover spends and the
chain checks its bytes alone; a certificate is valid whoever minted it. The
claims map, its lag state and the tests of remembering are deleted.

One transcript changes: spend-input-signer-missing-lifecycle drops from 174
to 94 transactions because chunks are reused instead of republished on each
CLI call.

245 files changed, 1192 insertions(+), 3070 deletions(-)

Ran: fault-proofs tsc (0 errors), eslint and prettier on changed files,
fault-proofs fast tier 6,984 passed, 0 failed, 3 skipped, 16 slow-tier files
74 passed, watcher fast tier 1,553 passed, the watcher installed journey.
Not run: the rest of the fault-proofs slow tier, Docker-backed suites.

Remove the hand-ported pstack skills; use the upstream plugin

The repository carried a rewritten copy of pstack 0.15.6 (52 skill
directories, a role configuration and a port README). Upstream now ships
its own build for the same host, so the copy and every local edit to it are
deleted. Install the current release with:

  /plugin marketplace add cursor/plugins
  /plugin install pstack@cursor-plugins

167 files deleted. The 19 Midgard skills are unchanged.

Ran: check-agent-skills (19 skills), check-doc-links, check-enforcement-tags,
check-agent-config, check-registry-paths, and the scripts/agents and
scripts/ci tests (169 passed).

Drop the tradeoff order; state that performance is highly important

The ranked list put performance below simplicity. The guide now names the
two kinds of failure and says performance is a product requirement.

Register the placeholder category id in the own-thread cancel plan test

The catalogue scan lists every category id written in the repository that
no family registers. The cancel-plan test uses ffffffff to prove no cancel
is planned for an unregistered id.

Delete the pending wait, the reconciliation-only mode and two mempool overlays

A workflow run that ends pending now returns pending; the supervisor's next
observation pass runs the job again. The loop that re-ran a pending workflow
every second for up to thirty minutes inside one supervisor turn is gone,
together with the harness clock and the two tests that existed for it.

Reconciliation-only mode had no production caller beyond the departure
completion check and the proof-materials sweep, which keep a permit that
carries no live fault and is revoked on rollback. The fresh-submission
refusal, the deadline-null job branch and the arms that served it are gone.

The mempool is decoded once, in @al-ft/midgard-l1-follower/mempool; the
provider and the workflow's next-state view both use that overlay. A listed
transaction that does not decode is skipped instead of failing the capture.

Also removed: the own-view `unseen` hook, the slot on the mempool listing
(Go sidecar, TypeScript transport, fake sidecar), the preflight-stall retry
that nothing called, and two duration entries for deleted tests.

131 files, +515 / -3,154.

Ran: tsc for l1-follower, l1-node-transport, fault-proofs, watcher and
node-tools (0 errors); eslint and prettier on changed files; go test in the
sidecar; l1-follower 740/740; l1-node-transport 35 passed, 4 devnet skips;
fault-proofs fast tier 6,993 passed, 0 failed, 3 skipped; watcher fast tier
1,553/1,553; the watcher installed journey.
Not run: fault-proofs and watcher slow tiers beyond the touched harness
files, devnet and Docker-backed suites.

Remove the goal spec; keep its protocol reference in docs/spec

docs/exec-plans/GOAL_SPEC.md was a program plan: work packages, acceptance
criteria and evidence rules, some of them mandating machinery that has since
been deleted. Its protocol content (the protocol decisions, the exact margin
thresholds and the per-family output contract) moves to
docs/spec/protocol-decisions.md as plain reference. The plan and its digest
are deleted.

References are repointed to the new file where they cite moved content, and
dropped where the comment already states the rule or cited a plan row. Aiken
and TypeScript changes are comments only: the blueprint built before and
after has the same 1,183 validators, byte for byte.

Also marks references in three old decision records to files deleted earlier
as historical, so the documentation link check passes.

Make simplicity a ranked tradeoff and put the burden of proof on complexity

The contributor guide ranked correctness, safety, liveness, performance and
convenience, and described every failure as a risk to funds. Nothing in it
pushed code out, so guards, records and alerts accumulated for failures of our
own process whose whole cost was a fee.

AGENTS.md now separates protocol failure from operational cost, ranks
simplicity after liveness, and states two principles: a mechanism stays only
when it names a realistic trigger and a protocol failure nothing else
prevents, and the preferred change is the one that deletes.
docs/agents/production-l2.md gives the four-part test a mechanism has to pass
and the facts that remove whole classes of handling (the chain and our node's
mempool are the record; our transaction cannot land script-invalid). The
consensus review skill gains an excess lens: code that fails the test is a
finding equal to a gap.

Always-loaded text shrinks: CLAUDE.md is a short router, the longest skill
descriptions are cut, and the skill check caps a description at 320
characters.

Derive fault-proof workflow progress from the ledger and the node's mempool

A transaction the workflow sent is in a block or in our node's mempool; if it
is in neither, the next pass builds it again. The workflow now reads that view
on every pass and keeps no record of what it sent.

The L1 node transport lists the node's mempool (LocalTxMonitor; frame protocol
version 3). The follower decodes the listed transactions and overlays them on
its ledger view, in the provider and in the fault-proof capture, at the node's
tip. Stage derivation uses the overlaid view: a target that is live on the
ledger but spent in the mempool is a pending stage, and the next action is
built on the pending outputs without waiting for a block. Evidence, completion
and finality stay ledger-only; validation-trace finality comes from the
capture's confirmation depth.

Deleted: the in-memory in-flight send set, coin holds, the absence rule, the
released-send follow, the restart wait and its readiness reason, the
wallet-only send gate, the three-minute wallet-only validity bound and its SDK
builder parameter, the fixed coin choice, signed-transaction recovery and
rebroadcast, and the resubmission hold with its readiness reason and alert.

Step transcripts are regenerated: rows lose the ttl the bound added, and later
rows move in the indices and validity windows that follow from earlier
transactions being built sooner.

Follow released in-flight sends and restore the pre-sign shape check

- An objective no run drives any more keeps what it sent in flight until
  the chain settles it: each completed pass at tip reads those
  transactions, settles the ones that landed final or can no longer land,
  and forgets the objective's part once nothing is left
  (workflow/in-flight-released.ts). Its coins are no longer held until
  restart, and a dead transaction no longer blocks an action waiting on
  an address it could have landed at.
- A transaction of another action leaves an expired predecessor's
  required coins held for that action, and only its rebuild is offered
  them.
- A proof-materials sweep that failed or was lost runs again at the next
  completed pass at tip while the views still hold sweepable materials.
- Before signing, the workflow wallet checks the transaction's shape from
  its bytes: outputs only to rostered contracts, our wallet and our
  proof-materials address; embedded scripts on the roster; collateral
  from and to our wallet; a fee our coins pay within the ceiling
  (workflow/transaction-shape.ts).
- The in-flight decoders free their CML objects.
- Funding helpers nothing in production read are deleted or moved to
  test support.

Replace the fault-proof workflow's stored record with chain-derived recovery

The workflow runner no longer writes or reads a crash journal. What a
restarted process needs it reads from the chain; what it must remember
between its own observations it holds in process memory.

Proof holds
Startup no longer releases a hold because a workflow execution is absent;
a verified completion still releases. A hold no objective owns is released
only in a completed admission pass at tip, once its header is out of the
finalized queue with its departure beyond k+1, and no held unit has a live
carrier (outside the fraud-proof spend address) or a move within k+1. A new
proof roster prune floor holds pruning at the follower origin until the
first pass at tip in the process and never drops once lifted. Prune floor
lags and the unowned and live-kept hold counts are reported as follower
degradations. The lost-defense slash-due read holds the receipt unit with
the case unit so a burned case token's history stays readable.

Own computation threads
Add a header-free cancel of our own computation threads, one per
registered family, derived from the family application registry, and a
watcher sweep that finds them from the L1 follower alone: live carriers
under the computation-thread policy whose step datum names our key,
paged under a fixed cap and classified against the tip and the block
finalDepth deep. A thread whose header is gone at both is cancelled
back to our wallet, after a recheck just before submission. The
supervisor's pump runs one bounded pass after the jobs of each admitted
observation.

The sweep reads no stored workflow record and keeps no durable state;
a cancel spends its thread, so it cannot land twice. Fees come from
wallet coins no funding reservation leases, held until the cancel's
validity ends. Operators see fault_proof_own_thread_unreclaimed and
fault_proof_own_thread_uncancellable as status-only degradations.

Proof materials
Each prover key gets one process-memory view of its proof-materials
address. Proof chunks, field carriage, transition-trace carriage and
script-decode staging resolve through it by exact inline datum, strictly
shaped and ordered by out-ref, so a restarted workflow finds its earlier
publication without the stored record. Workflows register what they need
and the dispute family pins its staging outputs. The end-of-workflow
sweep takes only strictly shaped outputs nobody needs, and no longer
holds the ending on sweep finality. The follower gains bounded plain-
output reads, and the watcher opens sweeping after the first admission
pass at its tip once every objective admitted by then has observed. The
field-preimage publication is funded from the largest plain coin alone,
so a rebuild over an unchanged wallet is the same transaction.

Dispute own view
The dispute finds its threads, pending claim, cases, record, receipts,
staging outputs and field publications from the chain view by prover
key, with the trace recomputed and checked against the claim and case
datums. Only "submitted by this process and not yet applied" still
comes from the workflow record, behind one port. Staging outputs a live
thread of ours still needs are held by recomputed plan datums from the
first observation after a restart, and outputs no move read are spent
back with the rest. A record on our key is our own: every live case of
ours plays to its close, nearest deadline first, and once our record's
removal completes the remaining cases still close. The ending waits on
no spend-back finality. Field-carriage certificates are found by token
and content. A wallet-only send held by the restart wait skips only
that action, and the objective stays admitted.

Stored record
- In-flight sends and the wallet coins they spend are held in memory
  (workflow/in-flight.ts, workflow/workflow-wallet.ts). The runner holds
  only on an in-flight transaction of the action the observation
  requires, and does not build an action inferred from an absent output
  while a transaction of ours may still land at that address.
- Reconcile, supersede, the funding reservation and funding runtime, the
  stored dispute view and the departed-header drive are removed. Under
  reconciliation-only authority the proof-materials sweep and the staging
  spend back are admitted by kind; nothing else is signed.
- A landed transaction of ours is final at release finality depth. When
  our removal makes the header depart, the objective completes from the
  chain at that depth and one sweep-only run collects its materials.
- Completion markers bind the removal transaction; older rows still
  parse. watcher.sqlite is no longer opened. The collateral accounting
  and forfeiture alerts, the workflowJournalDirectories option and the
  --workflow-journal-dir flag are gone.
- The dispute own view reuses admitted transactions and decoded staging
  reads between hops.
- The unused bound-data publication capability is deleted.

Tests that pinned only the deleted record are removed; the rest read
their state from the chain.
Remove an import the deleted committee store test left unused
